key_insight: An AI-assisted workflow for tissue-based neural autoantibody interpretation improved reader accuracy, especially for novice readers, and outperformed unaided interpretation in a prospective validation study.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help standardize autoimmune encephalitis antibody screening and reduce reader-dependent variability in pathology-style tissue interpretation.
method: Trained on 2,357 retrospective serum and CSF tissue-based assay images from >80 institutions
Prospectively tested on 200 new images from 200 patients using a binary classifier
Compared 2 expert and 2 novice readers in unaided vs AI-assisted rounds after a washout period
evidence_signal: In prospective validation, the standalone classifier achieved AUC 0.922, and AI assistance increased pooled reader accuracy from 90.4% to 97.4% with specificity rising from 82.6% to 99.5%.
watch_item: Results came from a centralized workflow and fixed-order reader study, so multicenter cross-platform validation is still needed before broad deployment.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
